rationale: Round 0 compiled and ran correctly, so headroom exists to push obfuscation on this tiny (702-byte text, 2-function) floating-point benchmark whose entire attack surface is the arithmetic-heavy main loop. SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain because arithmetic substitution directly obscures the FP kernels at low correctness risk and modest size cost, and the binary is so small that size growth is cheap. BCF and SPLIT are raised next: bogus predicates and block splitting add control-flow ambiguity, but BCF's RuntimeCost stays low-ish because bogus predicates execute on every iteration of a hot numeric loop. FLA is held at moderate security with a low RuntimeCost weight since flattening a tight FP loop carries the worst slowdown risk here, while IBR adds indirect branching diversity at acceptable cost. ICALL and IGV remain lowest-value: with essentially no indirect-call sites or global-variable traffic in a single-main flops kernel they yield little diversity, so they stay enabled only as low-weight options; correctness-risk weights are kept low across all passes to preserve the verified-correct behavior from round 0.
